# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first portrait browser game called **Chem Heat: Suburban Collapse** from this protected mechanic truth: a top-down driving chase loop with accelerate/brake/turn controls, tile collision, vehicle damage, score pickups worth +500, public-harm heat events worth +50 and +1 wanted/heat star, patrol pursuit at heat, game over at zero health, and restart.

Use the remix premise: Crime escalation strategy. A satirical game inspired by Breaking Bad with moral collapse, chemistry-driven schemes, cartel danger, suburban dread, transformation under pressure, dark irony, and consequence-heavy choices with mobile-first controls, touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, optimized on game start for portrait UI format, and the best-adapted mobile UX version targeting portrait aspect ratios in the 4:7 to 9:16 range.

The final surface should show a rolling chemistry-lab RV in a suburban/desert grid, reagent crates as rewards, police/cartel danger as hazards, RV Integrity/Lab Cash/heat-star HUD language, dark ironic copy, touch-friendly controls, and readable portrait UI. Preserve mechanics exactly; transform presentation boldly.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source identity
The preserved source is a self-contained portrait top-down vehicle chase game. The player drives a car through a generated block grid, collects cash, can hit pedestrians to increase wanted stars, takes damage on vehicle/wall contact, and loses when health reaches zero.

## Protected mechanics
- Four-way driving input: accelerate, brake/reverse, turn left, turn right.
- Vehicle physics: acceleration, friction, steering only while moving, speed caps.
- Tile map generation with road/building/open tiles.
- Collision model: walls bounce/damage, vehicle contact damages, pedestrian contact at speed scores and increases heat.
- Scoring: +500 pickup, +50 pedestrian heat event.
- Heat/wanted stars: 0-5 stars; police pursue when heat exists.
- State flow: start screen, active play, HUD/controls, game-over screen, restart.

## Safe transform surfaces
Title, copy, HUD labels, colors, vehicle silhouettes, pickup symbols, background colors, CSS atmosphere, audio naming notes, and progression framing are safe to transform.

## Rebuilt target
Chem Heat: Suburban Collapse reframes the same loop as a satirical rolling-lab escape about moral collapse and escalating consequences.
